set.typical_award_size: Conduit tax-exempt and taxable multifamily housing revenue bonds issued by the City Council on request under Council Policy 000-15 (RES-2018-071) and City Code Chapter 4-52; amounts set per project within CDLAC allocation (non-profit borrowers may not need an allocation). Bonds are non-recourse to the City and Housing Authority. Issuer fees per the Bond Policy Term Sheet: $5,000 non-refundable application fee (covers initial review and TEFRA hearing, credited at closing), issuance fee of 25 basis points of principal with a $20,000 minimum at closing, and annual compliance monitoring fee of 12.5 basis points of original principal paid semi-annually. Borrower pays all City, bond counsel, financial advisor, CDLAC, trustee and other costs. Rated issues need AA or better unless privately placed under Exhibit A.
set.affordability_requirement: Must satisfy CDLAC regulations and Section 142(d) (20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI minimum); Council may impose more restrictive terms per issue. Qualified Project Period set in each Regulatory Agreement (typically 15 years after 50% occupancy, or longer if bonds remain outstanding or CDLAC requires). Project must show positive cash flow after year one or cover any operating deficit for five years.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Bond Policy Exhibit A Section III.A(10) requires the borrower to comply with California Labor Code Section 1720 et seq. and indemnify the City, and to meet Davis-Bacon if any bond funds are federal (https://srcity.org/DocumentCenter/View/21065/Bond-Policy). This is a compliance covenant, not a determination that conduit bonds alone trigger prevailing wage, so the trigger stays unclear.
set.layering_notes: Alternative to CSCDA, CMFA or CalHFA conduit issuance for 4% LIHTC deals in Santa Rosa; using the City as issuer can simplify coordination with Housing Authority loans and regulatory agreements. The Developer Information page confirms the program and lists local funds (real property transfer tax and housing impact fees), CDBG, HOME and HCD funds used by the Housing Authority. The Bond Policy and Term Sheet were opened this pass (srcity.org DocumentCenter 21065 and 21066); contact is the Housing Trust Division, HousingTrust@srcity.org, (707) 543-3300. Whether the City is actively issuing versus deferring to JPAs was not confirmed.

reason: Bond Policy and Term Sheet opened and issuer fees and terms added; prevailing wage remains unclear because the policy only requires compliance with Labor Code 1720 where it applies.

set.typical_award_size: Regulatory. The City applies state density bonus law (Government Code 65915) through Implementing Zoning Ordinance Chapter 27, last updated in 2019; Zoning Code Interpretation 2023-01 (September 8, 2023) directs staff to apply state law wherever Chapter 27 conflicts until the code is updated. In November 2022 the City Council adopted a resolution exempting deed-restricted affordable housing projects from the City's facilities, parkland, traffic and open space impact fees (City Housing Finance Analysis, August 2023). Housing Element Program 14 committed the City to adopt by December 2023 a broader incentive package: expedited review, a dedicated project manager, Local Housing Trust Fund participation, density bonus beyond state law, and streamlined review for 100% affordable projects. Whether that package and any local bonus beyond state law were adopted could not be confirmed.
set.layering_notes: The November 2022 impact fee exemption for deed-restricted affordable projects is in effect per the City's 2023 Housing Finance Analysis and can count as a local match in state funding applications; confirm current exemption terms with Planning. set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Resolution 12-2020 established Affordable Housing Fees for Nonresidential Development, charged per gross square foot by nonresidential use type including additions; the rate schedule itself was not opened. The City's FY 2023-24 AB 1600 fee report shows the Affordable Housing Impact Fee account (732-00000-000-30120) collected $7,452.98 in FY 2023-24 with an ending balance of about $104,000 to $137,000 at June 30, 2024 (the report's summary and detail pages differ), no projects yet identified, and a plan to earmark funds in the FY 2025-26 budget. Housing Element Program 8 directs the City to adopt by December 2023 a per-square-foot impact fee on single-family homes and 2 to 4 unit projects and by December 2025 to expand the nonresidential fee after nexus studies. The FY 2023-24 report lists no residential affordable housing fee, so the residential fee had not been adopted as of June 30, 2024.
set.affordability_requirement: Fee proceeds go to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (Resolution 18-2019) for low and moderate income housing development, preservation, and loan and grant programs.

reason: Housing Element and the City FY 2023-24 fee report support the record; added fee account balance and confirmed no residential affordable fee existed as of June 2024.
